To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the complete N and E genes encoding proteins of a new human coronaviruses (HCoV- NL63) were successfully amplified from one of the pediatric patients with acute respiratory infection, the sequences were cloned and sequenced, the data predicted by computer were helpful for the further characterization of the new HCoV-Nl63.
the N and the E genes of HCoV- NL63 were successfully amplified, cloned and sequenced.

The complete sequences of BJ8081 N protein and E protein genes were amplified, cloned and sequenced, then the secondary structure and the characteristic of the proteins were predicted by computer software.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular characterization and bioinformatics analysis of N and E protein of HCoV- NL63.
the sequence analysis and bioinformatic prediction for the N and E gene encoding proteins of HCoV NL63 identified in Beijing.
the molecular characterization of HCoV- NL63, especially the analysis of the N and E proteins encoding genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HCoV-Nl63 is an important pathogen for acute respiratory tract infection.

the N and the E genes of HCoV NL63 were successfully amplified from clinical specimen, the recombinants plasmids were constructed and sequenced and the data predicted are helpful for the analysis and the research on HCoV-N63.
the N gene of HCoV- NL63 identified from sample BJ808 is a new human coronavirus, and the E gene is a new human virus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N and the E gene encoding regions of HCoV NL63 were successfully identified and sequenced, which will contribute to further study of HCoV.

the N and the E gene of HCoV identified in this study were similar to those of prototype HCoVs, and the recombinant N and E proteins of BJ8081 could be used as the antigen in ELISA for detection of HCoV infection.
the new HCoV-Nl63 was identified from one pediatric patient with acute respiratory infections in Beijing by bioinformatic methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the N and the E genes of HCoV NL63 were successfully amplified and cloned, the recombinants plasmids pUCm-T and pCF-T were successfully constructed and their sequences were submitted to Gen Bank, and the secondary structure and characteristics of the N and E proteins of sample BJ808 were predicted by bioinformatic analysis.
we have identified and characterized a new human coronavirus, which is the first case of human coronavirus infection in China.
the recombinant pCF-T- 8081 N and the pUCm-T -8081 E plasmids can be used as the vaccine vectors for HCoV-Nl63.
